statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer c with 0 <= c < n, r[c] is the number of unordered pairs {a,b} of vertices such that 0 <= a < b < n, a != c, b != c, dist(c,a) is divisible by signalSpeed, dist(c,b) is divisible by signalSpeed, and the simple paths from c to a and from c to b have no edge in common. Here dist(x,y) is the sum of the weights of the edges on the unique simple path between x and y in the tree formed by edges.
preconditions: Let n = len(edges)+1. The input satisfies: 2 <= n <= 1000; len(edges) = n-1; every edges[i] has length 3; writing edges[i] = [a_i,b_i,w_i], we have 0 <= a_i,b_i < n, a_i != b_i, and 1 <= w_i <= 10^6; the undirected graph on vertices 0,...,n-1 with one edge {a_i,b_i} of weight w_i for each i is connected and acyclic (so it is a tree); and 1 <= signalSpeed <= 10^6.
